messages:
mike: Quick question — current gateway behavior feels surprising. If a route defines a host capture like `*.{org}.example.com` and the path also defines `/{org}/...`, we end up with two captures for `org` and they get merged. Is that intended?
elaine: Oof, yeah that collision was the old impl. They canonicalize capture names by key which can cause host -> path overwrite. Not ideal.
jon: I remember we did that to make template substitution simpler for backends, but agreed it leads to confusion when host and path are semantically different.
mike: Example: ```route {
  host: "*.{org}.example.com"
  path: "/{org}/dashboard"
  service: "dashboard-svc"
}``` In practice we saw requests for `acme.example.com` -> `/acme/dashboard` and the router happily sets org=acme from host, fine. But if path is `/internal/{org}/...` you can get mismatched values.
rachel: Right, and worse: our logging/telemetry surfaces a single `org` label so it's hard to tell whether the value came from host or path. Ops ran into this during the SSO rollout.
mike: Proposal: make capture namespaces explicit. e.g. `host.{org}` vs `path.{org}` so they don't collide unless user explicitly aliases. Also surface a console warning when both captures with same name are used across host/path.
elaine: I like the explicit namespace idea. Implementation-wise, we could keep backward compatibility by treating unprefixed captures as before, but emit a deprecation/ambiguity warning.
jon: Another option: precedence rules. Host capture wins or path capture wins. But that still surprises people and hides where value came from. Explicit is clearer.
mike: UX for console: show both captures in the route editor with small badges: "host.org" and "path.org" and a tooltip "distinct capture sources; map to same backend variable?" with a toggle to map them.
rachel: Also add a telemetry tag for ambiguous captures: `route.capture_conflict=true` so we can query how often customers rely on the current merging behavior.
router-bot: Deploy bot: rule-checker ran on staging; 3 routes flagged for duplicate capture names (host vs path). See https://ci.internal/reports/2108765432/checks
elaine: Perfect — that report gives us concrete routes to test. For the schema change, we need to update route DSL docs and SDKs. Backwards compat: add `capture_namespace` opt-in in route v2, and emit warnings in API responses for v1 routes that would be ambiguous.
jon: Edge case: wildcard hosts with multiple captures like `*.{team}.{org}.example.com` and path `/org/{org}/team/{team}`. Users may want to map host captures to path captures intentionally. We should provide an explicit `alias` mapping in route metadata, e.g. `captures: {"host.org": "path.org"}`.
mike: Good call. Keep defaults conservative (no implicit aliasing), provide alias helpers in the console (autocomplete to map).
rachel: For matching precedence: we should avoid changing match semantics. This is purely about variable naming and visibility to backends. If we accidentally change which route wins, huge blast radius.
elaine: Agreed. Implementation plan: 1) Validator check + warnings (week 1) 2) Telemetry (week 1) 3) Console UI for explicit alias + badges (week 2-3) 4) SDK + docs (parallel) 5) Route v2 with namespaced captures and optional alias opt-in (week 4+)
mike: Is there any performance cost to namespacing? Parser changes only, runtime matching unchanged. Minor.
jon: Test plan: unit tests for parser, integration test hitting routes with conflicting values, rollout on dedicated clusters first.
mike: Ok cool. @rachel can you file an RFC/implementation ticket with the validator example from router-bot? I can draft the console mockups.
rachel: On it. I'll include examples and signal for telemetry.
mike: Thanks. :thumbsup:
